title: [YSQL] Possible database OID collision with system_postgres
body:
Jira Link: [DB-11504](https://yugabyte.atlassian.net/browse/DB-11504)
### Description

(1) Create a local cluster with the gflag --TEST_ysql_oid_prefetch_adjustment=49148
This gflag simulates the scenario that those OIDs < 65532 are already used so
the next OID to allocate starts from 65532 (16384 + 49148).

```
./bin/yb-ctl create --rf 1 --tserver_flags TEST_ysql_oid_prefetch_adjustment=49148
```

(2) Prepare the following test script:
```
cat /tmp/test.sql
CREATE DATABASE test0;
CREATE DATABASE test1;
CREATE DATABASE test2;
CREATE DATABASE test3;
\c test3
CREATE table t0 (id int);
CREATE table t1 (id int);
CREATE TABLE t(k SERIAL, v INT);
```

(3) Run the above test script
```
./bin/ysqlsh -a -f /tmp/test.sql
CREATE DATABASE test0;
CREATE DATABASE
CREATE DATABASE test1;
CREATE DATABASE
CREATE DATABASE test2;
CREATE DATABASE
CREATE DATABASE test3;
CREATE DATABASE
\c test3
You are now connected to database "test3" as user "yugabyte".
CREATE table t0 (id int);
CREATE TABLE
CREATE table t1 (id int);
CREATE TABLE
CREATE TABLE t(k SERIAL, v INT);
ysqlsh:/tmp/test.sql:8: ERROR:  Errors occurred while reaching out to the tablet servers
```

(4) Look into tserver log:
```
E0529 16:09:01.055245  8673 ql_expr_util.cc:59] Corruption (yb/qlexpr/ql_expr_util.cc:58): Column at 1 is not key column in Schema [
    0:ybrowid[binary NOT NULL HASH],
    1:id[int32 NULLABLE VALUE]
]
properties: contain_counters: false is_transactional: true consistency_level: STRONG use_mangled_column_name: false is_ysql_catalog_table: false retain_delete_markers: false partitioning_version: 1 ysql_replica_identity: CHANGE
```

(5) Root cause
The root cause of this error is that the database oid 65535 (0xffff) is reserved
by Yugabyte to store sequence table `system_postgres.sequences_data`, where
`system_postgres` called `namespace` in docdb, and `sequences_data` is the table name.

```
static const uint32_t kPgSequencesDataTableOid = 0xFFFF;
static const uint32_t kPgSequencesDataDatabaseOid = 0xFFFF;
```

`kPgSequencesDataDatabaseOid` is for `system_postgres`.
`kPgSequencesDataTableOid` is for `sequences_data`.

But 65535 is also a normal OID that can be allocated by the PG oid allocator. In
the test a user created database `test3` has already occupied the same OID 65535.
Further more, inside the user database OID 65535 was also allocated for table
`t1`. Later when the system tries to create the internal table
system_postgres.sequences_data, it collided with `test3.t1` which has a
different schema.
